statement: num_teams(rating) returns a result r, and r equals the number of index triples (i, j, k) with 0 <= i < j < k < n such that either rating[i] < rating[j] < rating[k] or rating[i] > rating[j] > rating[k]. Equivalently, r = |{ (i,j,k) : 0 <= i < j < k < n and ((rating[i] < rating[j] and rating[j] < rating[k]) or (rating[i] > rating[j] and rating[j] > rating[k])) }|.
preconditions: Let n = len(rating). The preconditions are: 3 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= rating[i] <= 100000; and for all 0 <= i < j < n, rating[i] != rating[j].

statement: For every rating satisfying the preconditions, num_teams(rating) returns a result r; in particular, the function never fails, overflows, or panics on any input in the precondition set.
preconditions: Let n = len(rating). The preconditions are: 3 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= rating[i] <= 100000; and for all 0 <= i < j < n, rating[i] != rating[j].

statement: Whenever num_teams(rating) returns a result r, r <= n*(n-1)*(n-2)/6, where n = len(rating). The right-hand side is the total number of index triples 0 <= i < j < k < n.
preconditions: Let n = len(rating). The preconditions are: 3 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= rating[i] <= 100000; and for all 0 <= i < j < n, rating[i] != rating[j].

statement: Whenever num_teams(rating) returns a result r, r is at least the number of indices i with 0 <= i <= n-3 for which the consecutive triple (rating[i], rating[i+1], rating[i+2]) is strictly increasing or strictly decreasing. In symbols, r >= |{ i : 0 <= i <= n-3 and ((rating[i] < rating[i+1] and rating[i+1] < rating[i+2]) or (rating[i] > rating[i+1] and rating[i+1] > rating[i+2])) }|.
preconditions: Let n = len(rating). The preconditions are: 3 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= rating[i] <= 100000; and for all 0 <= i < j < n, rating[i] != rating[j].

statement: Whenever num_teams(rating) returns a result r, r = 1 if (rating[0] < rating[1] and rating[1] < rating[2]) or (rating[0] > rating[1] and rating[1] > rating[2]), and r = 0 otherwise.
preconditions: len(rating) = 3; for every i with 0 <= i < 3, 1 <= rating[i] <= 100000; and rating[0], rating[1], rating[2] are pairwise distinct.

statement: Whenever num_teams(rating) returns a result r and rating is strictly increasing, i.e. rating[0] < rating[1] < ... < rating[n-1], then r = n*(n-1)*(n-2)/6.
preconditions: Let n = len(rating). The preconditions are: 3 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= rating[i] <= 100000; and for all 0 <= i < j < n, rating[i] != rating[j].

statement: Whenever num_teams(rating) returns a result r and rating is strictly decreasing, i.e. rating[0] > rating[1] > ... > rating[n-1], then r = n*(n-1)*(n-2)/6.
preconditions: Let n = len(rating). The preconditions are: 3 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= rating[i] <= 100000; and for all 0 <= i < j < n, rating[i] != rating[j].

statement: Let rev be the slice of length n defined by rev[i] = rating[n-1-i] for 0 <= i < n. Whenever num_teams(rating) returns a result r and num_teams(rev) returns a result r', we have r = r'.
preconditions: Let n = len(rating). The preconditions are: 3 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= rating[i] <= 100000; and for all 0 <= i < j < n, rating[i] != rating[j].

statement: Whenever num_teams(a) returns a result r and num_teams(b) returns a result r', we have r = r'.
preconditions: Let n >= 3 and let a and b be slices of length n. Both satisfy: for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= a[i] <= 100000 and 1 <= b[i] <= 100000; and for all 0 <= i < j < n, a[i] != a[j] and b[i] != b[j]. Additionally, for all 0 <= i, j < n, a[i] < a[j] if and only if b[i] > b[j].

statement: Whenever num_teams(b) returns a result r_b and num_teams(rating) returns a result r, we have r_b <= r.
preconditions: Let n = len(rating) with 3 <= n <= 1000, and assume rating satisfies: for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= rating[i] <= 100000; and for all 0 <= i < j < n, rating[i] != rating[j]. Let b be a slice of length m with 3 <= m <= n, and suppose there exist indices 0 <= t_0 < t_1 < ... < t_{m-1} < n such that b[q] = rating[t_q] for all 0 <= q < m.

statement: Whenever num_teams(rating) returns a result r, r > 0 if and only if there exist indices 0 <= i < j < k < n such that (rating[i] < rating[j] and rating[j] < rating[k]) or (rating[i] > rating[j] and rating[j] > rating[k]). Equivalently, r = 0 if and only if no valid team exists.
preconditions: Let n = len(rating). The preconditions are: 3 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= rating[i] <= 100000; and for all 0 <= i < j < n, rating[i] != rating[j].

statement: For each middle index j with 0 <= j < n, define L_<(j) = |{ i : 0 <= i < j and rating[i] < rating[j] }|, L_>(j) = |{ i : 0 <= i < j and rating[i] > rating[j] }|, R_<(j) = |{ k : j < k < n and rating[k] < rating[j] }|, and R_>(j) = |{ k : j < k < n and rating[k] > rating[j] }|. Then num_teams(rating) returns a result r, and r = sum over j = 0 to n-1 of (L_<(j) * R_>(j) + L_>(j) * R_<(j)).
preconditions: Let n = len(rating). The preconditions are: 3 <= n <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= rating[i] <= 100000; and for all 0 <= i < j < n, rating[i] != rating[j].
